nodes.content: Develop tactile slip prediction that distinguishes impending grasp slip from elastic deformation across unseen materials and sensor wear.
requirements: Predict slip at least 100 milliseconds ahead with ≥90% recall and ≤5% false-positive rate.
Meet targets on held-out materials and worn sensors, including deformation-only contacts matched for force.

nodes.content: Train a wear-invariant 100-ms slip-hazard model on viscoelastic-corrected tactile shear, contrasting force-matched deformation-only contacts.
Which viscoelastic-corrected shear features distinguish slip 100 ms ahead from force-matched elastic recoil under taxel wear?
Spatially propagating shear-residual fronts emerge ≥100 ms before slip but not force-matched recoil, even on unseen materials and worn taxels.
Run SlipRecoil-v1 leave-material-and-wear-out tests with force-matched recoil controls; measure ≥100-ms-ahead slip recall and deformation false-positive rate.
On SlipRecoil-v1, held-out materials and worn taxels showed propagating fronts: 92% slip recall at 100 ms, 3.8% deformation false positives.
Select propagating shear-residual fronts as the primary cue: held-out 100-ms recall reached 92% with 3.8% deformation false positives.
Implement the selected shear-front predictor; test 100-ms recall and false positives on unseen materials, worn sensors, and force-matched recoil.
Train ShearFront-v1, calibrate its threshold on validation contacts, then measure 100-ms slip recall and recoil false positives on held-out materials/wear.
ShearFront-v1 package contains the trained checkpoint, validation-calibrated threshold, and held-out material/wear report of 100-ms recall and recoil false positives.
Blind-test ShearFront-v1’s frozen checkpoint and threshold on unseen-material, worn-sensor slip and force-matched recoil trials; measure 100-ms recall and false-positive rate.
Blind ShearFront-v1 testing yielded 91% 100-ms slip recall and 4.2% false-positive rate on unseen materials, worn sensors, and force-matched recoil.
Noise-normalized shear-residual persistence over 40 ms distinguishes impending slip from force-matched recoil ≥100 ms ahead despite taxel wear.
Ablate shear-front features in SlipRecoil-v1; test 40-ms persistence alone on held-out materials, worn taxels, and force-matched recoil.
On SlipRecoil-v1 unseen-material/worn-taxel held-outs, persistence alone yielded 83% 100-ms slip recall and 11% force-matched recoil false positives.
Adding noise-normalized 40-ms persistence to ShearFront-v1 should cut worn-taxel recoil false positives below 4% while retaining ≥90% 100-ms recall.
After persistence-only’s 11% false-positive rate, test fused ShearFront-v2’s 100-ms recall and recoil false positives on unseen-material/worn-taxel contacts.
ShearFront-v2 achieved 92% 100-ms slip recall and 3.1% force-matched recoil false positives on held-out materials and worn taxels.
Can viscoelastic baseline calibration preserve ShearFront-v2’s 100-ms sensitivity after additional taxel wear without labeled slip trials?
Calibrate per-taxel viscoelastic baselines using 60-second unlabeled stationary grips; test frozen ShearFront-v2 across wear stages and force-matched recoil.
Record 60-second stationary-grip baselines across wear stages; recalibrate taxels and blind-test frozen ShearFront-v2 on unseen-material, force-matched slip/recoil trials.
WearCal-v1 bundles per-taxel baseline corrections and blind-test 100-ms recall and recoil false-positive reports by material and wear stage.
With unlabeled WearCal-v1 calibration, ShearFront-v2 achieved 91% 100-ms recall and 3.7% recoil false positives across unseen materials and wear stages.
Train a physics-guided state-space model separating reversible strain from irreversible interfacial creep using force-matched negatives and wear augmentation.
Can force-conditioned tactile relaxation distinguish interfacial creep from reversible strain before slip when material stiffness and taxel gain change?
Force-normalized irreversible-creep latent rises ≥100 ms before slip but remains low during force-matched recoil across unseen materials and wear.
Using WearCal-v1 corrections, train CreepState-v1; test creep-latent 100-ms recall and force-matched recoil false positives across unseen materials/wear.
WearCal-v1-corrected CreepState-v1 achieved 91% 100-ms slip recall and 4.4% force-matched recoil false positives on unseen-material/worn-taxel trials.
Retain ShearFront-v2 as primary over CreepState-v1: both meet targets, but false positives are 3.1% versus 4.4%.
Retain ShearFront-v2 for alerts; ablate CreepState-v1’s creep latent across stiffness and taxel-gain shifts against force-matched reversible strain.
Stratify force-matched SlipRecoil-v1 trials by stiffness and taxel gain; ablate CreepState-v1’s creep latent, measuring 100-ms recall and recoil FPR.
CreepAblate-v1 report tabulates creep-latent ablations, 100-ms slip recall, and force-matched recoil FPR by stiffness and taxel gain.
Re-score ShearFront-v1’s frozen checkpoint and threshold on CreepAblate-v1 stiffness/gain strata; compare 100-ms recall and force-matched recoil FPR.
On unseen-material, worn-taxel high-stiffness strata, CreepState-v1 achieved 90% 100-ms recall/4.5% force-matched recoil FPR versus ShearFront-v1’s 85%/7.2%.
Using WearCal-v1, compare ShearFront-v2 and CreepState-v1 across unseen-material stiffness/wear strata; measure 100-ms recall and force-matched recoil FPR.
On low-stiffness unseen materials and worn taxels, CreepState-v1 yielded 84% 100-ms recall and 8% force-matched recoil FPR; ShearFront-v2 achieved 92%/3.6%.
Keep ShearFront primary: v1 met overall targets, while CreepState’s high-stiffness advantage over v1 does not offset low-stiffness failure.
Force- and stiffness-normalized creep-to-recovery ratios should achieve ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% recoil FPR on low-stiffness worn-taxel contacts.
Train CreepState-v2 with stiffness-normalized creep-to-recovery ratios; test 100-ms recall and force-matched recoil FPR on low-stiffness worn-taxel contacts.
On low-stiffness, unseen-material worn-taxel contacts, CreepState-v2 reached 88% 100-ms recall and 6.1% force-matched recoil FPR, missing both targets.
Does stiffness-estimation error or overlapping bulk-relaxation and interfacial-creep trajectories cause CreepState-v2’s low-stiffness failure?
On CreepState-v2’s failed low-stiffness trials, substitute measured stiffness; assess slip–recoil latent overlap, 100-ms recall, and force-matched recoil FPR.
Substituting measured stiffness raised CreepState-v2’s low-stiffness 100-ms recall to 91% and reduced force-matched recoil FPR to 4.7%.
Probe contacts with 25-Hz subthreshold tangential micro-dither; predict slip from impedance phase lag versus force-matched recoil after wear calibration.
Collect 25-Hz micro-dither phase; apply WearCal-v1 and validate 100-ms slip recall and force-matched recoil FPR across held-out materials/wear.
With WearCal-v1 corrections, record 25-Hz dither impedance on unseen-material/worn-taxel slip and force-matched recoil trials; fit phase-lag classifier.
DitherPhase-v1 contains wear-corrected 25-Hz impedance traces, phase-lag classifier weights, and force-matched slip/recoil trial labels.
Blind-test DitherPhase-v1’s frozen classifier on held-out materials and wear; measure 100-ms recall, force-matched recoil FPR, and dither-induced slips.
Blind DitherPhase-v1: 93% 100-ms recall, 4.1% force-matched recoil FPR across held-out materials/wear; zero dither-induced slips in 300 recoil trials.
Keep WearCal-v1-calibrated ShearFront-v2 primary; reserve DitherPhase-v1 for uncertain contacts, trading 3.7% versus 4.1% FPR for 91% versus 93% recall.
Gate 25-Hz dither to WearCal-v1-calibrated ShearFront-v2 probabilities within 0.1 of threshold; retest 100-ms recall and recoil FPR.
Trigger DitherPhase-v1 within ±0.1 of ShearFront-v2’s calibrated threshold; blind-test 100-ms recall, recoil FPR, and dither exposure across materials/wear.
DitherPhase-v2 replaces always-on probing with ShearFront-v2 uncertainty gating; bundles WearCal-v1 corrections and blind-test recall, recoil-FPR, and dither-exposure reports.
Sweep 25-Hz dither amplitudes on held-out materials and worn sensors; measure phase separation, 100-ms recall, recoil FPR, and induced slips.
On low-friction worn-sensor contacts, safe-amplitude dither gave 84% 100-ms recall and 8% recoil FPR; higher amplitudes induced slips.
Suppressing dither on low-friction worn-sensor contacts should let WearCal-v1-calibrated ShearFront-v2 achieve ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% recoil FPR.
Disable DitherPhase-v2 probing on low-friction worn contacts; blind-test WearCal-v1-calibrated ShearFront-v2’s 100-ms recall and force-matched recoil FPR.
On blind low-friction, worn-sensor trials with dither disabled, ShearFront-v2 achieved 91% 100-ms recall and 4.3% force-matched recoil FPR.
Revive gated dither outside low-friction worn contacts; disabling it there yielded 91% 100-ms recall and 4.3% recoil FPR.
Can safe 25-Hz phase lag resolve borderline ShearFront-v2 slip/recoil decisions across unseen materials and worn sensors outside low-friction contacts?
Outside low-friction contacts, gated 25-Hz phase lag should deliver ≥90% 100-ms-ahead recall and ≤5% recoil FPR on borderline decisions.
Blind-test DitherPhase-v2 on borderline non-low-friction unseen-material/worn-sensor contacts; measure 100-ms recall, force-matched recoil FPR, and dither-induced slips.
On borderline non-low-friction held-outs, DitherPhase-v2 achieved 92% 100-ms recall, 4.2% force-matched recoil FPR, and zero induced slips.
Adopt revived gated dither outside low-friction contacts (92% recall/4.2% FPR); retain ShearFront-v2 inside (91%/4.3%), avoiding CreepState’s low-stiffness failures.
